header:
Carry a balance
to build credit?

lines.text: 48% of people believed this credit card myth (2023 survey).
lines.say: Forty-eight percent of people believed this credit card myth.

lines.text: The myth: carrying a balance builds your credit. It doesn't, and believing it gets expensive.
lines.say: The myth is that carrying a balance builds your credit. It doesn't, and believing it gets expensive.

lines.text: FICO, the company behind the score, says so too.
lines.say: FICO, the company behind the score, says so too.

scene.headline: FICO: No need to carry a balance for your score

lines.text: Your card reports your statement balance anyway. Pay it in full, and it still shows usage, with $0 interest.
lines.say: Your card reports your statement balance anyway. Pay it in full, and it still shows usage, with zero interest.

lines.text: Carry it instead, and you pay up: cards charged interest averaged 22.15% in Q2 2026 (Fed).
lines.say: Carry it instead, and you pay up: cards charged interest averaged twenty-two point one five percent in the second quarter of twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: On a $2,000 balance, that's about $37 a month, and your score gains nothing.
lines.say: On a two thousand dollar balance, that's about thirty-seven dollars a month, and your score gains nothing.

lines.text: In September 2026 the Fed raised rates a quarter point, and most card rates are variable.
lines.say: In September twenty twenty-six, the Fed raised rates a quarter point, and most card rates are variable.

lines.text: What counts: paying on time (35% of a FICO Score) and owing little (30%).
lines.say: What counts is paying on time, which is thirty-five percent of a FICO score, and owing little, which is thirty percent.

lines.text: Interest paid isn't on the list at all.
lines.say: Interest paid isn't on the list at all.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

scene.tagline: Pay interest for zero points? Myth.

post.title: Does Carrying a Credit Card Balance Build Credit? No.
post.ig:
48% of people believed this credit card myth.
The myth: carrying a balance builds credit (U.S. News survey, February 2023).
FICO calls it a myth: your score doesn't track whether you carry a balance month to month.
Cards charged interest averaged a 22.15% rate in Q2 2026 (Fed G.19). On $2,000, that's about $37 a month.
What counts: payment history (35% of a FICO Score) and amounts owed (30%).
Sources: Federal Reserve G.19, myFICO, CFPB, U.S. News & World Report.
News and education, not financial advice.
